B. Is this measure already running in Pirkanmaa wellbeing services county (or in the Tays university hospital area that treats its patients)?
A. Does recent evidence support the size of effect we assume: does this measure reduce deaths among the people it reaches, and by how much?
Measure: Smoking cessation started at the first specialist visit. Every current smoker with suspected lung cancer gets cessation medication and counselling at the first visit, as part of preparing for curative treatment.
effect_summary_en: One Moscow observational cohort of 517 current smokers with early-stage NSCLC found that those who quit after diagnosis had lower all-cause mortality (adjusted HR 0.67, 95% CI 0.53–0.85).
supported_en: Sheikh et al. (Annals of Internal Medicine 2021) report an adjusted all-cause mortality HR of 0.67 (95% CI 0.53–0.85) for quitting after diagnosis.
not_supported_en: The pages read do not show that offering cessation help at the first visit produces this effect: the study compared people who quit with people who kept smoking, it did not test an offer of help, it is observational, and it was done in Moscow.
in_use_quote: Kysymme jokaiselta potilaalta tupakka- ja nikotiinituotteiden käytöstä ja kirjaamme tiedot hoitokertomukseen. Tupakoiva potilas saa tukea tupakoinnin lopettamiseen ja hänelle tarjotaan vierotushoitoa.
in_use_summary_en: Pirha's Tays hospitals ask every patient whether they smoke and offer cessation treatment to smokers. Under the 'Tupakoimattomana leikkaukseen' model, Tays asks patients to stop smoking as soon as surgery starts being planned, and the lung cancer pathway page says smoking is assessed at the specialist visit.
missing_en: No page shows that every smoker with suspected lung cancer gets cessation medication and counselling at the first specialist visit as a standing order.
summary_en: Part of this measure already runs. Pirha's 'Savuton sairaala' page says Tays asks every patient whether they smoke and offers cessation treatment to smokers. It also runs a 'Tupakoimattomana leikkaukseen' model that asks patients to quit as soon as surgery starts being planned, and Pirha's lung cancer pathway page says smoking is assessed at the specialist visit. On the effect, one observational study (Annals of Internal Medicine 2021) found that early-stage lung cancer patients who quit after diagnosis had lower all-cause mortality than those who kept smoking (adjusted HR 0.67, 95% CI 0.53–0.85). That matches the assumed number, but it compares quitters with continuing smokers rather than testing an offer of help.
unanswered_en: I found no page showing that cessation medication is started at the first specialist visit for every smoker with suspected lung cancer, and no page saying how many patients quit. I did not use the two search rounds still allowed to look for this.
